::: proof
Subtracting the constant $\mu$ does not change a covariance,
and covariance is bilinear, so:

$$
\ba
\Cov{Y_{ijk}, Y_{i'j'k'}}
&= \Cov{L_i + B_{ij} + \epsilon_{ijk},\ L_{i'} + B_{i'j'} + \epsilon_{i'j'k'}}
&& \text{(subtract the constant } \mu \text{)}
\\
&= \Cov{L_i, L_{i'}} + \Cov{B_{ij}, B_{i'j'}} + \Cov{\epsilon_{ijk}, \epsilon_{i'j'k'}} + R
&& \text{(bilinearity of covariance)}
\\
&= \Cov{L_i, L_{i'}} + \Cov{B_{ij}, B_{i'j'}} + \Cov{\epsilon_{ijk}, \epsilon_{i'j'k'}}
&& \text{(} R = 0 \text{)}
\ea
$$

where $R$ is the sum of the six cross covariances,
such as $\Cov{L_i, B_{i'j'}}$,
each between two independent random variables,
so each is 0.

Each remaining covariance is a variance when its two arguments are the same random variable,
and 0 when they are different, independent random variables:

- $\Cov{L_i, L_{i'}}$ is $\sigma_L^2$ if $i' = i$ and 0 otherwise;
- $\Cov{B_{ij}, B_{i'j'}}$ is $\sigma_B^2$
if $(i', j') = (i, j)$ and 0 otherwise;
- $\Cov{\epsilon_{ijk}, \epsilon_{i'j'k'}}$ is $\sigma^2$ if $(i', j', k') = (i, j, k)$ and 0 otherwise.

Adding the terms that are nonzero in each case gives @eq-nested-re-cov.
:::
